description: baseline torch.geqrf compact QR

Replace torch.geqrf for small and medium square batches with a CUDA C++ extension implementing batched Householder QR in-place, targeting n<=512 with one matrix per block/CTA family and falling back to torch.geqrf for larger or numerically risky cases.
Tried torch.utils.cpp_extension CUDA Householder QR for n<=512, but validation JIT failed because ninja is unavailable in the runtime environment.
Manual nvcc-built Householder QR extension validates for n<=512, but full geomean regressed because the 640x512 cases are much slower than torch.geqrf.
Limited manual CUDA Householder path to n<=352; validation passed but benchmark geomean still regressed versus baseline due to small-shape overhead and fallback noise.

Restricted manual CUDA path to only the 32x32 batch; validation passed, but full benchmark geomean remained slightly slower than baseline, suggesting the custom kernel does not beat torch.geqrf enough even on tiny matrices.

Added a warp-specialized 32x32 Householder QR kernel and dispatch only for n=32; validation passed and benchmark geomean improved versus baseline while all larger and risky cases fall back to torch.geqrf.

Best result is commit 5b566279c63b65a4be624f136e5e22c4b16d4dc6 with qr_v2 geomean 113871779.353 ns versus 116056332.369 ns baseline. Successful idea: a manual nvcc-built CUDA shared library with a warp-specialized Householder QR kernel only for the 20x32 benchmark, falling back to torch.geqrf for all larger or risky shapes. Generic one-CTA Householder kernels for n<=352 and n<=512 validated but regressed badly/mostly broke even, so future work should avoid per-matrix CTA QR for 512 and instead investigate batched library/panel approaches or combine this n=32 dispatch with other workers overhead reductions.

Preserve eight-stream 80-matrix geqrf batching for 640x512, graft the n==32 warp-specialized CUDA QR fast path, resolve dispatch ordering so shape predicates are disjoint, keep existing fallbacks, and benchmark each active shape to disable any regressing route.

Combined the proven n=32 warp CUDA QR path with the eight-stream 80-matrix torch.geqrf chunks for batch=640,n=512 using disjoint shape predicates; validation passed and full geomean improved to 105096017 ns.
Kept the combined n=32 warp route and increased 640x512 torch.geqrf chunking from 8 to 16 streams of 40 matrices; validation passed and geomean improved to 92611091 ns.
Increased 640x512 chunking to 32 streams of 20 matrices while preserving the n=32 warp QR route; validation passed and geomean improved to 66385059 ns.

Best result is commit c95b76f70ab4e19decbf608e28704c77e27a5d69 with qr_v2 geomean 66385058.843 ns. Combined both parent wins: n=32 warp-specialized CUDA QR and streamed torch.geqrf for 640x512, then tuned 512 chunking; 8 streams measured 105096017 ns, 16 streams 92611091 ns, 32 streams 66385059 ns, while 40 and 64 streams regressed to 67328397 ns and 72262278 ns. Disabling n=32 or 512 routing also regressed, so the final disjoint dispatch keeps n=32 custom QR, batch=640/n=512 with 32 chunks, and torch.geqrf fallback for all other active shapes.

Target remaining large QR shapes batch=8,n=2048 and batch=2,n=4096 with guarded stream-chunked or batched large-shape routes, sweep chunk counts, stream counts, and row/column partitioning, preserve existing 640x512 and 60x1024 fast paths byte-for-byte, profile first, and keep only non-regressing correct routes.

Added guarded stream-chunked torch.geqrf routes for batch=8,n=2048 with 8 chunks and batch=2,n=4096 with 2 chunks, preserving existing 640x512 and 60x1024 fast paths unchanged; validation passed and geomean improved to 38232081 ns.

Best result is commit 4eabcd43c1955a5d6882a2db553a2f1ea409b48a with qr_v2 geomean 38232080.703 ns. Added guarded stream-chunked torch.geqrf routes for the remaining large shapes: batch=8,n=2048 uses 8 chunks and batch=2,n=4096 uses 2 chunks, while preserving the existing 640x512 and 60x1024 fast paths byte-for-byte. Sweeps showed n=2048 at 16 chunks (38246307 ns) and 4 chunks (39779391 ns) regressed versus 8, n=4096 at 4 chunks regressed (38313769 ns), and disabling either 2048 or 4096 route regressed (43885107 ns and 40223608 ns). Full final nsys timed out, but focused nsys profile for 2048/4096 was saved for the final commit.

Reduce tiny-shape overhead without new CUDA by optimizing n=32 Python dispatch, predicate order, exact stream/geqrf path selection, and avoiding torch.cat/split/chunk work on small paths; preserve existing n=176, n=352, n=512, n=1024, n=2048, and n=4096 stream routes and benchmark all active shapes.

Tried micro dispatch reordering with early n=32 fallback and batch-grouped predicates, preserving all stream route counts, but the wrapped build/validate/benchmark sequence terminated before producing metrics.

Retried the committed dispatch micro-reorder separately; validation passed and benchmark geomean improved slightly to 30229465 ns by early-returning n=32 and grouping exact stream-route predicates by batch while preserving all route counts.

Replaced nested exact route predicates with a module route dictionary lookup while preserving all chunk counts. Validation passed but geomean regressed to 30260130 ns versus the grouped predicate dispatch, so this route-map variant is not preferred.
Restored the best grouped predicate dispatch after route-map regression, preserving the prior measured geomean 30229465 ns.
Bound torch.geqrf to a module global for n=32 and fallback dispatch. Validation passed but geomean regressed to 30263786 ns, so the direct torch.geqrf calls in grouped dispatch are preferred.
Restored the best grouped predicate dispatch after global geqrf binding regressed, preserving the measured best geomean 30229465 ns.

Best result is commit 50ef80f4deea1057d1e90d53ccd00857211a6fe4 with qr_v2 geomean 30229464.913 ns. Micro tuning kept all n=176,n=352,n=512,n=1024,n=2048,n=4096 stream routes and optimized tiny/dispatch overhead by early-returning n=32 and grouping exact predicates by batch. Route-map lookup regressed to 30260130 ns and global geqrf binding regressed to 30263786 ns, so both were rejected/restored. A focused n=32 nsys profile was saved for the final best commit.

Reduce stream-chunked output assembly overhead by replacing torch.cat/list aggregation with preallocated H/tau outputs plus slice copies or out buffers where safe, preserving n32 CUDA and exact current chunk routes and counts, benchmarking all active shapes, and keeping only non-regressing variants.

Replaced list aggregation and torch.cat in stream-chunked QR routes with preallocated H/tau outputs and per-chunk slice copies, preserving n32 CUDA and all current route counts. Validation passed; geomean improved to 27673027 ns.

Changed stream-chunked QR assembly to call torch.geqrf with out=(H slice, tau slice), removing intermediate per-chunk tensors while preserving n32 CUDA and all current route counts. Validation passed; geomean improved to 27510825 ns.

Best result is commit 984ee775ebb94c91ab5b83e0a09b5cdd4c2dcbdb with qr_v2 geomean 27510825.088 ns. Replaced stream-chunked torch.cat/list output assembly first with preallocated slice copies (27673027 ns), then improved further by calling torch.geqrf with out=(H slice, tau slice), preserving n32 CUDA and exact current chunk routes/counts. Focused n352 nsys profile saved for final commit; broader 3-shape nsys run returned 143 without report generation.

Preserve global-best out= slice assembly and all tuned routes, graft only the n4096 chunk=4 route from the large-shape branch, benchmark same-run against n4096 chunk=2 under out= assembly, and keep it only if it improves the primary metric.

Grafted only the n4096 chunk=4 route onto the out= slice assembly parent, preserving all other tuned routes. Validation passed but full geomean regressed to 27626701 ns versus parent 27510825 ns, so n4096=4 is rejected.
Restored the global-best out= slice assembly parent with n4096 chunk=2 after the grafted n4096=4 route regressed, preserving the measured parent metric 27510825 ns.

Best result remains the out= slice assembly leader, restored at commit b12358ee1d78f238296dc8dd49d78534086ab207 with qr_v2 metric 27510825.088 ns from parent 984ee775. The only requested graft, n4096 chunk=4, validated but regressed to 27626700.830 ns under out= assembly, so it was rejected and n4096 chunk=2 was restored. Existing focused profile artifacts for the out= leader 984ee775 remain available and no new route is kept.

Micro-optimize Python stream orchestration only: specialize or hoist per-shape stream lists and route metadata to reduce launch-helper overhead while preserving out= assembly, n32 CUDA, and all chunk counts; benchmark all active shapes and keep only non-regressions.

Hoisted route metadata and replaced data.chunk with computed slicing while preserving route counts and out= assembly. Validation passed but full geomean regressed to 27566374 ns, so this broader orchestration change is rejected.

Simplified _chunked_geqrf stream-pool key to omit len(chunks), preserving data.chunk routes and out= assembly. Validation passed but full geomean regressed to 27651975 ns versus parent 27510825 ns, so this micro change is rejected.

Bound torch.cuda.stream and torch.geqrf to local variables inside _chunked_geqrf while preserving stream pools, chunk counts, data.chunk, and out= assembly. Validation passed but full geomean regressed to 27597462 ns versus parent 27510825 ns, so this micro change is rejected.

Changed _chunked_geqrf loop to zip streams with chunks, preserving data.chunk, stream pool keys, chunk counts, and out= assembly. Validation passed but full geomean regressed to 27680941 ns versus parent 27510825 ns, so this micro change is rejected.

Brief 6 exhausted. Tested three additional narrow Python stream-orchestration micro changes after the broader hoist: stream-pool key simplification (27651974.942 ns), local binding of torch.cuda.stream/geqrf (27597462.145 ns), and zip(streams,chunks) loop shape (27680940.584 ns). All validated but regressed versus parent/global best 984ee775 at 27510825.088 ns, so final HEAD is restored to 984ee775 with no new kept optimization. Existing profile for the parent remains applicable.

Preserve one-warp n32 CUDA and out= stream routing and assembly exactly, graft only n512=30 and n1024=9 chunk counts from the tuning branch, then same-run benchmark against parent and keep only on primary metric improvement.

Grafted only n512=30 and n1024=9 chunk counts onto the one-warp n32 CUDA parent, preserving stream out= assembly and all other routes. Same-run parent measured 26125652.124 ns; candidate validated and improved to 25207960.586 ns, so this combine is kept.

Graft only the fully unrolled one-warp n32 CUDA kernel onto the current best, preserving n512=30, n1024=9, out= assembly, and all existing routes; same-run benchmark against parent and keep only if the primary metric improves.

Grafted only the fully unrolled one-warp n32 CUDA kernel onto current best, preserving n512=30, n1024=9, out= assembly, stream routing, and all other chunk counts. Same-run parent measured 25200073.638 ns; candidate validated and improved to 25188915.225 ns, so this combine is kept.
